beats.text: Joseph Swan showed a working lamp in 1879.
beats.note: Wikipedia says that on 3 February 1879 he publicly demonstrated one to over seven hundred people. The lamp usually cited as Edison's first success was made on 19 October 1879.

beats.name: Newcastle Chemical Society
beats.role: Where Swan lectured, before showing the lamp in actual operation on 17 January 1879.

beats.text: His home was the first with working bulbs.
beats.note: Wikipedia says Underhill, Low Fell, Gateshead was the world's first house to have working light bulbs installed.

beats.text: His British patent came in November 1880.
beats.note: Wikipedia gives British Patent 4933 on 27 November 1880. The IET adds that Swan had not sought a patent covering his lamp in general terms.

beats.text: Edison went to court in Britain.
beats.note: Grace's Guide says he brought an infringement case over Swan's patent and lost, and had to take Swan in as a partner in his British works.

beats.name: Ediswan
beats.role: The Edison and Swan United Electric Light Company, formed by merging the two British companies.

beats.text: In Britain, the company name carried both inventors.
